A_general.open_code_note: No official Quartr MCP repository or package was found in the collected sources. The community repository listed in links.json is unofficial and was not used as evidence.
other_official_servers: https://quartr.com/docs/mcp is the product documentation page. https://quartr.com/docs exposes a separate documentation-site MCP with documentation search and feedback tools; it is not the product server analyzed here.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MCP access is included with a Quartr Pro subscription. Student plans are ineligible. The vendor does not publish a price on the pricing page; it directs customers to sales.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Quartr Pro pricing is described as scalable for multi-seat deals; prices are not published. Enterprise deal options are available.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: No separate MCP per-call charge is documented. The endpoint documents user-level request limits per tool and across all tools.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A valid Quartr account and OAuth authorization are required. Read-only authorization exposes only read-only tools. Documentation describes two combined limits: 100 requests/minute, 2,250/hour, and 8,500/day. Per-tool limits shown in the tool reference range from 20 to 100 requests/minute.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls subscription eligibility, endpoint authorization, and rate limits. The user chooses read-only access at consent or requests the mcp:read scope. Microsoft 365 access is also controlled by the Microsoft 365 admin.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official reference lists 47 tools spanning user information, companies, events, conferences, documents, summaries, financials, reference data, watchlists, keywords, saved items, workspaces, and search filters. The reference labels tools Read-only, Write, or Destructive and gives per-tool request limits.
The product reference does not document MCP resources. A separate docs-site MCP mentions resources, but it is a different server and is not evidence for this endpoint.
No product-server prompts are documented in the collected official product reference.
The product documentation reviewed does not describe MCP call logging, user-visible audit records, or telemetry settings.
No sampling capability is documented for the product server.
No roots capability is documented for the product server.

Endpoint POST evidence: HTTP 401, WWW-Authenticate Bearer realm="mcp", resource_metadata="https://mcp.quartr.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", scope="mcp:tools". Protected-resource metadata at both the origin and endpoint path reports resource_name "Quartr MCP Server", bearer_methods_supported ["header"], scopes_supported ["mcp:tools","mcp:read"], and authorization_servers ["https://mcp.quartr.com"]. Authorization-server metadata reports authorization_endpoint /oauth/authorize, token_endpoint /oauth/token, registration_endpoint /oauth/register, revocation_endpoint /oauth/revoke, response_types_supported ["code"], grant_types_supported ["authorization_code","refresh_token"], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["none"], code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"], scopes_supported ["mcp:tools","mcp:read"], resource_indicators_supported true, and revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["none"]. The product docs state OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, support client ID metadata documents or dynamic client registration, and say tokens are refreshed automatically. They state tokens are scoped to mcp:tools by default and users can request mcp:read for read-only access. The authorization-server path-suffix metadata and token lifetime were not provided.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated endpoint returned HTTP 401 and {"error":"Unauthorized"}. Product documentation describes 429 responses with Retry-After for combined-limit breaches and tool error results containing error: "rate_limited" and retryAfterSeconds for per-tool breaches.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration; client ID metadata documents; OAuth 2.0 authorization code and refresh token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth method none; Bearer token in header; scopes_supported: mcp:tools, mcp:read; revocation endpoint /oauth/revoke, revocation auth method none. Token lifetime not stated. Raw endpoint challenge: Bearer realm="mcp", resource_metadata="https://mcp.quartr.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", scope="mcp:tools".

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The docs describe read-only selection on the OAuth consent screen; no MCP Elicitation capability is documented.
No MCP Tasks capability is documented.

The endpoint uses Streamable HTTP. The docs say it is stateless, requires no session ID, and uses JSON responses. Read-only access is available through the consent screen or mcp:read scope; the endpoint then exposes only tools marked Read-only.
Rate-limit errors are documented. A general MCP error-reporting capability is not described.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: 429 with Retry-After for combined limits; per-tool error result with error: "rate_limited" and retryAfterSeconds. Other error formats are not documented.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The server documentation requires an eligible Quartr Pro subscription, but does not describe MCP subscription notifications or a subscription capability.
No progress notifications or progress-tracking capability are documented.
No cancellation capability or behavior is documented.

No initialize instructions for the product endpoint were found in the public product documentation. Tool descriptions include task guidance, including a preference for standardized financial figures on numeric questions and a preferred append mode for workspace edits.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools are explicitly labeled Read-only, Write, or Destructive in the official reference; no individual readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations are documented. 2. No confirmation parameter or approval workflow is documented for writes. Read-only consent is a scope-level access restriction, not confirmation for individual actions. 3. OAuth scopes are mcp:tools and mcp:read; docs say read-only access exposes only tools marked Read-only. No product-role inheritance, admin switches for the hosted endpoint, client allowlist, or token lifetime is documented. Token revocation is documented at /oauth/revoke; metadata says revocation auth method none. 4. Read-only mode is documented. No toolset URL/header filters, sandbox endpoint, or regional product endpoint found. 5. No MCP-specific PII masking or data-boundary behavior documented. 6. Per-tool limits are shown in the tool reference; combined limits are 100/minute, 2,250/hour, 8,500/day per user. Some tools paginate or cap results; examples include list_events max 200, search results up to 100, and write_workspace max 200 top-level blocks. read_document returns chunks; long transcript reads support timestamp windows. 7. The tool reference describes parameter requirements, enums, ranges, and some validation constraints. No general unknown-argument rejection or argument correction is documented. 8. MCP audit logging and telemetry are not documented. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, report, or upsell tool appears in the official product tool list. 10. No server-delivered skill tool is documented. Tool descriptions contain behavioral guidance but the public server code is unavailable to establish enforcement. 11. Persistence is evident for user-owned watchlists, keyword alerts, saved items, folders, workspaces, and search filters; no evidence that prior agent behavior changes outputs or available tools. Workspace edits are live to connected users and prior state snapshots are documented. 12. The product endpoint is documented as one stateless Streamable HTTP endpoint. 13. The official tool list contains no raw API, SQL, or arbitrary script escape-hatch tool.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Prefer this over transcript or summary tools for any numeric or financial-figure question
so confirm the period in the report before treating it as a single quarter.
Use this to answer who presented at or what happened at a named conference.
Prefer `append` unless the user asked for a full rewrite.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented product endpoint is a single stateless Streamable HTTP server. A separate documentation-site MCP exists, but it is not part of this endpoint.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference at https://mcp.quartr.com/docs names 47 tools; the page has no stated total. actions.json contains all 47 official names. One additional catalogue-only name, read_live_transcript, appears in the Claude connector directory listing of 38 tools and is not in the current official list; it is therefore marked third-party with default status unknown. The Claude listing says 38 tools; Manufact reports 38; Agent Discoverability reports 47; MCP.so says its tool list is unavailable; Tedix lists tool names but no total. These catalogue counts/listings differ from the 47 names in the official reference.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim initialize and complete tool-definition payload was found for this endpoint; the documentation list is not a serialized tools/list response.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The product pages advertise AI chat, live earnings-call audio, consensus estimates, event calendars, transcript highlighting, slide history comparison, and export of custom datasets. These product capabilities were not found among the 47 MCP tools in the official reference. Sources: https://quartr.com/mcp?source=banner and https://quartr.com/pricing.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions provide guidance, including “Prefer this over transcript or summary tools for any numeric or financial-figure question” and “Prefer `append` unless the user asked for a full rewrite.” These are tool-description instructions; without public implementation code, whether the server enforces them is not established.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The product documentation says read-only connections expose only tools marked Read-only, so the AI cannot create, change, or delete listed research assets. Workspace edits automatically snapshot prior state for reversion in version history. The vendor states the MCP is for individual subscribers' own research workflows and directs product builders to the Public API.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The product page describes the data as first-party IR material published directly by public companies and says it contains no news feeds, broker research, or third-party content. MCP access is included with Quartr Pro.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata and documentation support the existence of authorization and read-only scopes. The official tool reference marks read-only and write/destructive operations, but no public implementation code was found to verify authorization filtering, workspace snapshots, or other server-side enforcement. Data provenance and product-purpose claims are documentation statements; technical verification was not available.

contradictions: The current official reference lists 47 tools, while the Claude connector directory and Manufact list 38; the Agent Discoverability catalogue reports 47. The Claude listing includes read_live_transcript, which is absent from the current official list, while the official list includes additional tools not shown by the 38-tool directory listings.

The OAuth protected-resource metadata lists both mcp:tools and mcp:read. The product documentation describes mcp:tools as the default scope and mcp:read as read-only access; it does not explain whether mcp:tools is strictly read/write or whether other authorization rules apply.
observations_for_research: The documented read-only configuration is enforced through OAuth consent or scope selection and changes which tools are exposed, rather than relying only on the client to refrain from writes.

Several tool descriptions give workflow preferences and cautions that can steer agent choices, including preferring standardized financial data for numeric questions and checking report periods for year-to-date cash-flow values.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, pages/INDEX.txt, official product docs and page scripts, tool reference, pricing page, and collected catalogues. The official GitHub repository list was empty; the listed community GitHub server is unofficial and was not used as evidence. No official privacy-policy page or MCP-specific retention, training, logging, token-lifetime, or complete initialize/tools/list payload was present in the collected evidence. The separate https://quartr.com/docs/mcp page describes the documentation-site MCP, not the product endpoint.
